notes.2ii: Many candidates did not appreciate that a change in temperature required two thermometer readings, so the error was often not doubled.
notes.2c: This question proved challenging for most candidates. A majority ticked the correct box (temperature rise would be approximately the same); most of those explained their answer in terms of doubling the mass of zinc, FA 3, as well as the volume or moles of FA 1. The doubling of the mass of zinc was to ensure it remained in excess so it did not become relevant. Only a small minority gave answers linking the doubling of heat energy evolved with the doubling of volume of solution to heat.
notes.2d: A large minority of candidates omitted this part. Candidates should be reminded to label the arrows on any Hess cycle they construct with the relevant value from their calculations or from the default values given in the question. notes.3a: Many candidates recorded the expected colours in the reaction of FA 4 with aqueous potassium iodide followed by aqueous sodium thiosulfate. A number of these reported a precipitate where there should be none or an incorrect colour of the sulfur precipitate slowly formed with the thiosulfate. Very few candidates reported the initial yellow colour of FA 4 and many only gave the final colour. Candidates should be aware that adding a solid to a solution is not forming a precipitate. A higher proportion of candidates reported effervescence but many did not identify it as hydrogen.
notes.3i: Candidates should be reminded that the term ‘redox’ should be used where a species in a reaction is oxidised or reduced as one cannot occur without the other. Some candidates described the type of reaction as displacement or neutralisation or exothermic, so did not link their answer to the colour changes they observed in (c).

notes.key_messages: • Candidates should avoid the early rounding of intermediate answers during calculations. • Candidates are reminded that observations for a chemical reaction should focus on the physical changes that take place. • The use of the Data Booklet should be encouraged for questions involving infra-red spectra. • When a question asks for a name of a reagent(s) then the formula of reagent(s) is not acceptable. General comments
notes.general_comments: General comments The majority of candidates were able to finish the paper within the hour allowed. Questions 1, 21, 30, 34 and 39 were found to be more challenging to candidates. Comments on specific question The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. From the Data Booklet the element is gallium. When three electrons have been removed, the electronic configuration of the Ga3+ ion is 1s22s22p63s23p63d10. The third shell is full at this point.
